note: Import-check thresholds (docs/SPEC.md 6.1.4, 6.1.5). Checks only measure and report; they never modify files and never trigger a conversion (A-12, D-030). Values marked 'practice' are conventions subject to calibration; 'decision' values are fixed defaults that may still be edited here.

length_mismatch.note: Differences up to max(0.5 s, 0.5 % of the longest length) pass with a warning (trailing-silence trims). Larger differences suggest mixed renders and are rejected; alignment is asked, never time-stretched.

silence.note: A stem whose samples are all exactly zero or whose peak stays below the threshold is reported as a failed export. Import still records it; the user decides to drop it or re-export.

clipping.note: A run is consecutive samples at or above clip_level_abs on one channel. Float files may legitimately exceed 1.0; that is reported separately as over-full-scale.

head_click.note: Largest sample-to-sample jump in the first window_ms (including the jump from silence to the first sample) compared with the high percentile of jumps in the following reference_ms.

headroom.message: likely master-bus processed (little headroom and low peak-to-loudness ratio)
headroom.note: A mix for mastering should keep headroom without loudness maximising. The fallback (sample peak and RMS crest factor) is used only when the loudness module is unavailable.

stem_sum.note: Plain sum of all stems at gain 0, head-aligned at the project rate, compared with the bundled full mix: null residual in dB relative to the full mix and Pearson correlation. AI service stem exports often do not sum to their full mix, so this is never a reject; it feeds the mastering route choice (SPEC 6.6.1).
